shared.title: Clone from shared
shared.subtitle: Ready-built projects maintained by admins — clone one instead of rebuilding knowledge.
shared.notReady: Not ready — no knowledge built yet

overview.calloutTitle: Project Knowledge powers every AI workflow
overview.calloutBody: Before analysing requirements, generating test cases, or writing Playwright, Q‑Agent reuses what it learned about this repository — architecture, page objects, fixtures and conventions.

knowledgeTab.emptyBody: A project can hold many repositories, each with its own knowledge base. Add the repos this project owns, then build knowledge per repo.

businessTab.title: Business Knowledge
businessTab.subtitle: What the product is supposed to do — the rules, the vocabulary and the decisions a test case is written from. A peer of Project Knowledge, which describes how it is built.
businessTab.emptyBody: Test cases are written from your product's rules and vocabulary — add the documents that describe them. A requirements page, a domain glossary, a policy document, a decision log: anything that says what the product must do rather than how it is coded.

addressHint.url: One page is fetched, once. Links on it are not followed, and no credential is used.
addressHint.github_md: A repository, a folder, or a single .md file — paste the address as it appears in the GitHub URL bar.
addressHint.ado_wiki: Paste the address of any page in the wiki you want. Every page under it is fetched.

upload.hint: This version accepts .md and .txt files only, up to 10 MB each. The file is read and stored as you add it, so there is nothing to sync afterwards.

github.publicNote: A public repository needs no token at all. Attach a GitHub connection only if the repository is private — its token needs the contents:read scope.
github.hubNote: This connection is managed by EmeHub, which never releases its token, so the repository is read anonymously. That is fine for a public repository; a private one will report that it may be private and needs contents:read.
github.refNote: A branch name containing a slash, such as release/2024, is read as its first segment only — a GitHub web address cannot tell that apart from a folder. Link the folder on a branch without a slash, or link the file itself.

ado.testFailed: That token could not read the wiki
ado.hubRefusal: Wiki pages can't be read through the shared EmeHub connection — it never releases its Azure DevOps token. Add a wiki-scoped token for this project.
ado.missing: This Azure DevOps wiki needs a token. Add a personal access token with Wiki (Read) scope above, or pick a connection that holds one.
ado.connectionNote: This source will use the connection's token. If the sync fails with a scope error, add a wiki-scoped token above instead — a connection made for work items carries no Wiki (Read) scope.
ado.sourceNote: This token is stored encrypted on this source alone, and is never shown again.

businessTab.pendingNote: Registering a source does not fetch it. A new link starts fetching as soon as it is added, and “Sync now” on any row fetches it again — the row’s status is the fetch.
businessTab.excludedHint: Kept for provenance, but no longer fed into new test cases.
businessTab.deleteMessage: “{{title}}” and its stored snapshot are removed for good. To stop it grounding new test cases without losing it, exclude it instead.
businessTab.noProject: This project is still resolving — business sources load once it has.

facts.title: Facts and corrections
facts.subtitle: What the documents distilled into, and your overlay on it. A correction never edits the original — it supersedes it, so where your team and the document disagree stays visible.
facts.empty: Nothing distilled yet. Sync a source above, or add a fact the documents never stated.
facts.excludedHint: Out of context. It stays here, and one click brings it back.
facts.addHint: A fact your documents never stated. It outranks anything distilled from them, and a re-sync will not touch it.
facts.correctHint: Your correction supersedes “{{term}}”. The original stays below, struck through, so the disagreement with the source is visible.
facts.editHint: Editing your own fact. The revision counter moves; the ingested facts are untouched.

repoKnowledge.buildingBody: Cloning the repo and analysing the source — this can take a few minutes. You can leave this page; it keeps running.
repoKnowledge.notIndexedBody: Build this repository's knowledge base so Q‑Agent learns its routes, selectors, auth flow and conventions before generating tests.
repoKnowledge.needsRefresh: This repository changed since the last index. Rebuilding its knowledge base is recommended.

intro.title: Every ticket, case and run in this project follows these connections
intro.body: The ticket source is set once, here. No screen lets you switch provider mid-flow.

ticketSource.label: Ticket source
ticketSource.purpose: The only place this project's tickets come from

codeKnowledge.label: Code & knowledge
codeKnowledge.purpose: Repository and pull requests feeding Project Knowledge and automation

testCase.label: Test case target
testCase.purpose: Where approved cases are created, linked and results published

connectionTab.noEligible: No eligible connections — add one in Settings

hubManaged.title: Managed by EmeHub
hubManaged.body: EmeHub owns this project's configuration. Q-Agent shows it read-only — open the project in EmeHub to change it.
hubManaged.bodyNoLink: EmeHub owns project configuration here, so Q-Agent shows it read-only. This project isn't linked to an EmeHub project yet; manage it in EmeHub.

manualLogin.noLoginLocalAgent: No saved login yet — capture now and a browser opens on your Local Agent, or it opens automatically on the first run.
manualLogin.noLogin: No saved login yet — capture one now, or a browser will open on the first run.
manualLogin.capturingLocalAgent: A browser is opening on your Local Agent — log in there, then close the window to finish.
manualLogin.capturingHost: A browser opened on this machine — log in, then close the window to finish.

settingsForm.providerConnectionsDesc: Bind this project to a work-item source (where its tickets come from) and a repository source (where its code lives) — chosen independently. Manage connections in Settings.
settingsForm.applicationDesc: The default application URL the generated Playwright automation targets.
settingsForm.manualLoginDesc: Open a real browser on the host so an operator can log in before the run starts.
settingsForm.manualLoginNote: Before a run, a real browser opens on the machine running Q‑Agent so you can log in (e.g. Microsoft Entra); the session is reused until cleared.
settingsForm.testAccountsDesc: Credentials used by generated specs. Passwords are encrypted at rest and never shown — leave the password blank to keep the stored one.
settingsForm.environmentsDesc: Per-environment URLs. A run picks the environment matching its name (e.g. Staging).
settingsForm.name: Name
settingsForm.additionalSettingsDesc: Arbitrary project-specific key/values the automation generator can reference.

repos.bindProviderFirst: Bind a repository provider above first
repos.blurb1: Each repository gets its own knowledge base (built from the Project Knowledge tab). The
repos.blurb2: default repo is the one automation targets when a run doesn't specify one. Repos are cloned/pulled to
repos.blurb3: (private repos use the provider PAT), or use a local path if set.
repos.cloneUrlPlaceholder: clone URL (https://…) — used when no local path is set

automation.emptyBody: Q-Agent creates one the first time a run generates specs for this project.
automation.scaffoldOnlyTitle: Scaffolded but no generated files yet
automation.scaffoldOnlyBody: The repo exists and its skeleton is committed, but no run has generated anything into it. You can still download the scaffold.
automation.selectFileTitle: Pick a file to read it
automation.selectFileBody: Nothing is loaded until you open it — the tree carries paths only, and each file's code is fetched when you select it.
automation.repoNote: Your clone of a repo shared across your projects: automation repos are per-user, and one repo is keyed by provider project and repo name — so it may also hold files that other projects' runs created.
automation.noSpecsNote: No generated specs in this repo yet — the page objects, fixtures and data below are still real, accumulated work.
automation.loadFailedTitle: Couldn't load this project's automation repos
automation.loadFailedBody: The request for this project's automation repos failed. Nothing has changed on disk.
automation.treeFailedBody: The repo is there, but its file list could not be read.
automation.fileFailedBody: The file is listed in the tree, but its contents could not be read.

provenance.title: Generated by
provenance.openRun: Open this run's Automation stage for this case
provenance.historyToggle_one: {{count}} earlier run also wrote this file
provenance.historyToggle_other: {{count}} earlier runs also wrote this file
provenance.historyNote: A later run rewrote this path. Each earlier run kept its own copy of the spec it generated, so those rows are still on the record — they are simply no longer the code on disk.
provenance.superseded: Superseded by {{runCode}} — this run's stored spec is not the code on disk.
provenance.sharedTitle: Shared asset — reused and extended across runs. Q-Agent does not record which run last edited it.
provenance.gitNote: The repo's own git history does hold the per-commit answer; exposing it over HTTP (git log --follow) is a follow-up, not part of this view.

runSuite.description_one: Execute the {{count}} selected spec out of this repo, in parallel
runSuite.description_other: Execute the {{count}} selected specs out of this repo, in parallel
runSuite.noneSelected: Nothing selected — tick the specs you want to run in the tree
runSuite.sharedRepoNote: {{selected}} of {{total}} specs in this repo are selected. This repo is shared across your projects, so specs another project's runs generated are listed here but are not selected.

report.title: Playwright report
report.absent: This execution stored no Playwright report. Reports are kept from the moment an execution finishes with the JSON reporter configured, so older executions have none.
report.failedBody: The Playwright report for this execution could not be read. Try again, or re-run the suite.
report.noAttempts: Playwright recorded no attempt for this test.
